blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it

findings.evidence:
export const bucket = (ps: Price[]) =>
  ps.reduce<Record<string, Price[]>>((a, p) => ((a[(p.cents >> 4) & 0x3e8 ? "hi" : "lo"] ||= []).push(p), a), {});
findings.recommendation: Replace the one-liner with a plain function: a named constant `PREMIUM_THRESHOLD_CENTS = 1000` (10 euros, the premium band of the proposal), a loop or two `filter` calls comparing `price.cents >= PREMIUM_THRESHOLD_CENTS`, and an explicit return type such as `{ cheap: Price[]; premium: Price[] }` instead of `Record<string, Price[]>` keyed by the bare strings "hi" / "lo". Name the parameters (`prices`, `groups`, `price`) instead of `ps`, `a`, `p`. A reader cannot tell from `(p.cents >> 4) & 0x3e8` where the premium band starts — it is not "10 euros and more": 500 cents gives `31 & 1000 = 8`, truthy, so a 5-euro price lands in "hi", while the docstring promises a cheap/premium split. The shape is what hides this; the simple comparison would make the threshold, and any defect in it, visible. Callers also cannot know the keys without reading the expression, and a group with no price is absent from the result rather than empty.
findings.title: `bucket` packs its threshold into a bitwise one-liner nobody can read
